doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Managing and leading Dinah Washington's group
summary: Cobb was Dinah's manager and the band was billed under his name; he was told he looked too young.

bands.name: Dinah Washington and the Jimmy Cobb Band

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So we go Earl Bostic, and that leads you to . . .
With her, you did more than play drums, in the sense of the band, right?
Yeah. We were supposed to be married at that time. That’s what that situation was. We was . . .
But you had other responsibilities. Take the social part out.
I was supposed to be the manager.
I was supposed to be the manager, because I remember some people telling me, “You look too young to be a manger.” I’d say, “Well, it happens like that sometimes.” I

was a bandleader at one time. She made me a bandleader. Had “Dinah Washington and the Jimmy Cobb Band.” That’s what she did with her guys, I guess. I can’t fight it. So that’s what I was, a manager. I remember somebody like – what’s the popular singer, popular white singer – she told me – she says, “You look too young to be a manager.” I say, “You know what? That’s what I am.” Somebody’s got to be it. I’m here.
No, it wasn’t Rosemary. Somebody like that, though. It was . . .
Patti Page, yeah. Patti Page say, “You look like – you don’t look old enough to be a manger.” I say, “Yeah, well, I guess I don’t, but I am.”
